region.text: the whole of the former Portuguese colony of Mozambique

ledger.note: 25 June 1975: Mozambique becomes independent from Portugal as the People's Republic of Mozambique. 'Mozambique became independent from Portugal on 25 June 1975.'; infobox 'People's Republic of Mozambique: 25 June 1975 - 30 November 1990'.

region.text: the Gorongosa region of central Mozambique, RENAMO's base and headquarters until August 1985

ledger.note: 30 May 1977: the Mozambican Civil War begins (infobox 'Date: 30 May 1977 - 4 October 1992'). The only ground the page names for RENAMO is the Gorongosa region: 'RENAMO subsequently started operating in the Gorongosa region' (undated) and 'the capture of RENAMO headquarters at Gorongosa in central Mozambique in August 1985'; by the mid-1980s 'FRELIMO was unable to adequately defend most regions except the most important cities'. The zone is Sofala, the province of Gorongosa, by the researcher's reading; the page dates no wider zone. The low-level insurgency 'in the northern provinces of Zambezia, Tete and Niassa from 1977' is the Revolutionary Party of Mozambique's, not RENAMO's, and is not drawn.

30 November 1990: the People's Republic of Mozambique ends. Infobox 'People's Republic of Mozambique: 25 June 1975 - 30 November 1990'; 'The new constitution, enacted in 1990, provided for a multi-party political system' and 'Mozambique abolished the people's republic as the country's official name'. The state and its outline continue as the Republic of Mozambique.

region.text: the Gorongosa region of central Mozambique, the one RENAMO base the page names, at the end of the war on 4 October 1992

ledger.note: 4 October 1992: the Rome General Peace Accords end the civil war. 'On 4 October 1992, the Rome General Peace Accords' were signed and 'formally took effect on 15 October 1992'; a UN force of 7,500 arrived and elections were held on 27-28 October 1994. RENAMO had proposed 'a peace agreement based on the secession of RENAMO-controlled northern and western territories'; none was granted.

wars.name: Mozambican Civil War

zones.text: the Gorongosa region of central Mozambique, RENAMO's base

wars.outcome: Ended by the Rome General Peace Accords of 4 October 1992 (effective 15 October); no border changed and RENAMO's proposal of secession 'of RENAMO-controlled northern and western territories' was not taken up. Rhodesia was RENAMO's founder and backer to 1979 ('From 1975 to 1979, Rhodesian troops and forces repeatedly entered into Mozambique', including 'the occupation of the town of Mapai in 1977' and 'the bombing of the Beira Port in 1979'); 'After 1980, South Africa became RENAMO's main supporter'; Malawi deployed troops from April 1987 to defend the rail line.
wars.note: Infobox 'Date: 30 May 1977 - 4 October 1992'. RENAMO-controlled areas 'included up to 50% of the rural areas in several provinces' (Mozambique page), not located by the pages. The Nkomati Accord with South Africa is named but not dated.

wars.name: Cabo Delgado insurgency
wars.outcome: Ongoing at the end of the dossier: the Mozambique page records 'the outbreak of a violent insurgency in the northern province of Cabo Delgado beginning in October 2017' and says nothing of ground held.
wars.note: No zone: the page does not say the insurgents held territory, and the war is not drawn.

certainty.note: Judgement, not read in the pages opened: the frontiers are colonial treaty lines inherited at independence and no border dispute is recorded on the Mozambique page ('the page mentions no border dispute' with Malawi or Tanzania). Government control outside the cities was weak in the civil war (1977-1992), but no line was redrawn.

notes: Two pages only (budget 1-2 for 2 shapes). NOT SETTLED: (1) RENAMO: the Mozambican Civil War page dates the war to 30 May 1977 - 4 October 1992 but names RENAMO ground only as the Gorongosa region (operating there 'subsequently', undated; headquarters captured August 1985); the Mozambique page says RENAMO-controlled areas 'included up to 50% of the rural areas in several provinces' without naming them, and the civil-war page says RENAMO 'was able to carry out raids virtually anywhere in the country except for the major cities'. The contest zone is therefore drawn as Sofala (Gorongosa's province) for the whole war, which under-draws the war after the early 1980s; a gap-filler should open the Mozambican Civil War article's sections on the 1980s or the Gorongosa and RENAMO pages for provinces by year. The northern insurgency in Zambezia, Tete and Niassa 'from 1977' on the page is the Revolutionary Party of Mozambique's (founded 1974 or 1976 per the page), a different group, and is not drawn. RENAMO is named as a string and listed in the report as a counterpart that may need a rebel dossier (suggested slug renamo; no page opened gives a boundary or capital). (2) Rhodesian incursions ('From 1975 to 1979, Rhodesian troops and forces repeatedly entered into Mozambique', the occupation of the town of Mapai in 1977 and the bombing of Beira in 1979) have no end date for the occupation, so no occupation event is written; the rhodesia dossier (another part) may carry them. (3) The 1975 keyframe is new: Cliopatria's Mozambique shape begins 1976 although independence was 25 June 1975. (4) The renaming of Lourenco Marques as Maputo is not dated on the page. (5) The Lusaka Accord (7 September 1974) and the independence war (25 September 1964 - 8 September 1974) belong to the portuguese-mozambique dossier. (6) Cabo Delgado since October 2017 is a war entry with no zone; a gap-filler should open its own page for the insurgents' held towns, which this page does not give. No ruler strip: the page opened gives no list of presidents.
